I think the most fascinating part isn't just the display but the mechanical robustness of integrating 20,000 electrical connections into a flexible textile. Most previous attempts at smart clothing failed because the solder joints cracked under repeated bending and washing, so this laser-assisted wetting technique for precise micro-chip attachment seems like a genuine materials science breakthrough rather than a gimmick.

I wonder if the heat dissipation from 5,000 chips running simultaneously on an arm would actually be comfortable during extended use. The article mentions machine washability but doesn't explicitly clarify whether the power source needs to remain external or if it was integrated into the fabric itself in this prototype stage.
